name: SEAI Better Energy Homes
valueSummary: Up to €25,000 depending on works carried out
description: Grants for homeowners to improve the energy efficiency of their home. Covers insulation, heat pumps, solar panels, windows and doors across a range of individual measures.
keyRequirements: Home must have been built and occupied before 2011
Must use an SEAI-registered contractor
Works must not have started before grant approval
Must be the registered owner of the property

name: SEAI One Stop Shop
valueSummary: Up to €25,000 — same grant values as Better Energy Homes, with full project management included
description: An end-to-end managed retrofit service where SEAI-registered providers handle everything from assessment to installation. Ideal if you want a whole-home upgrade without managing contractors yourself.
keyRequirements: Home must have been built and occupied before 2011
Works carried out by an SEAI-registered One Stop Shop provider
Provider manages surveying, design, contractor procurement and grant claim
Must be the registered owner of the property

name: Help to Buy (HTB)
valueSummary: Up to €30,000 or 10% of the purchase price (whichever is lower)
description: A tax rebate for first-time buyers purchasing a newly built home or self-building. You get back income tax and DIRT paid over the previous four years, up to €30,000.
keyRequirements: Must be a first-time buyer (all purchasers on the mortgage must qualify)
Property must be a new build or self-build — not a second-hand home
Purchase price must not exceed €500,000
Must take out a mortgage of at least 70% of the purchase price
Must live in the property for 5 years after purchase

name: First Home Scheme
valueSummary: Equity stake of up to 30% of the property value — bridges the gap between your deposit and what you can borrow
description: A shared equity scheme where the government and participating banks take an equity stake in your home to help you bridge the gap between your mortgage and the purchase price. You buy back the equity over time.
keyRequirements: Must be a first-time buyer or 'fresh start' applicant
Must be purchasing a new-build property
Property price limits apply and vary by county
Must have a mortgage approval from a participating lender
Must contribute maximum deposit and borrowings before the scheme tops up

name: Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant
valueSummary: Up to €50,000 for vacant properties, up to €70,000 for derelict properties
description: A grant to refurbish long-term vacant or derelict properties for use as your principal private residence. Aimed at bringing empty properties back into use across Ireland.
keyRequirements: Property must be vacant for at least 2 years
You must intend to live in the property as your principal residence
Property must be in need of refurbishment
Application made to your local authority
Funding released in stages as work is completed

name: Croí Cónaithe (Cities) Scheme
valueSummary: Indirect benefit — government subsidises developers to make city apartments viable for owner-occupiers
description: A €450m government scheme that pays subsidies to apartment developers in Dublin, Cork, Limerick, Galway and Waterford to bridge the construction viability gap. The grant goes to the developer, not to you — but the result is more apartments available to buy at viable prices in cities. As of mid-2025, contracts were signed for over 1,000 apartments with more in progress.
keyRequirements: No direct application for individual buyers — the scheme operates at developer level
Apartments built under this scheme are for owner-occupiers, not investors
Located in Dublin, Cork, Limerick, Galway or Waterford city areas
Check with individual developers or agents whether a specific new apartment scheme received Croí Cónaithe funding

name: Warm Homes Scheme
valueSummary: Free — fully funded energy upgrades for eligible low-income households
description: Provides free energy upgrades to homeowners who receive certain social welfare payments. SEAI manages the programme and assigns an approved contractor at no cost to you. As of January 2025, fossil fuel boilers (oil/gas) are no longer covered — the scheme now focuses on insulation and renewable heating (heat pumps).
keyRequirements: Must be a homeowner receiving a qualifying social welfare payment (e.g. Fuel Allowance, Living Alone Allowance)
Home must be in need of energy upgrades
Works are fully funded — no contribution required from homeowner
SEAI assigns contractor — you do not need to find one
Fossil fuel boiler replacements are no longer covered (renewable heating only since Jan 2025)

name: Solar PV Grant
valueSummary: Up to €1,800 depending on system size (€600 per kWp, max 3 kWp)
description: A grant towards the cost of installing solar photovoltaic (PV) panels on your home to generate your own electricity. Any surplus can be exported to the grid under the Microgeneration Support Scheme.
keyRequirements: Home must have been built before 2021
Must use an SEAI-registered solar contractor
Works must not have started before grant approval
Must be the registered owner of the property

name: Heat Pump Grant
valueSummary: Up to €12,500 — €6,500 for the heat pump, €2,000 for heating upgrades, plus €4,000 renewable heat bonus if replacing a fossil fuel system (increased February 2026)
description: A grant to replace your existing heating system with a heat pump (air-to-water, ground source, or exhaust air). The grant nearly doubled in February 2026 and now includes a bonus for replacing oil or gas boilers. Heat pumps are highly efficient and can significantly reduce heating bills.
keyRequirements: Home must have been built and occupied before 2021
A technical assessment is required before installation
Home must meet minimum insulation standard (or insulation must be upgraded first)
Must use an SEAI-registered contractor
Works must not have started before grant approval
€4,000 renewable heat bonus applies when replacing an existing fossil fuel (oil/gas) system

name: Window & Door Upgrade Grant
valueSummary: Up to €5,600 — up to €4,000 for windows, plus €800 per external door (max 2 doors). Significantly increased March 2026.
description: A grant towards the cost of upgrading windows and external doors to improve the energy efficiency of your home. Grant values were significantly increased in March 2026 — nearly tripling the previous window allowance.
keyRequirements: Home must have been built and occupied before 2011
Must use an SEAI-registered contractor
New windows must meet minimum U-value standard
Home must have adequate attic and wall insulation already in place
Works must not have started before grant approval

name: Local Authority Home Loan
valueSummary: Fixed-rate mortgage up to €320,000 (€350,000 in Dublin, Cork, Galway, Kildare, Meath, Wicklow)
description: A government-backed, low fixed-rate mortgage for first-time buyers who cannot get sufficient mortgage approval from a commercial bank. Offered by local authorities at competitive rates.
keyRequirements: Must be a first-time buyer (or fresh start applicant)
Must have been refused or insufficient mortgage from two banks
Gross annual income must be under €70,000 (single) or €85,000 (joint)
Property must be your principal private residence
Property value limits apply by county

name: Local Authority Purchase and Renovation Loan
valueSummary: Combined loan up to €500,000 — covers purchase price plus renovation costs
description: A low fixed-rate loan from your local authority to buy and renovate a vacant or derelict property. Combines the purchase mortgage and renovation finance into a single loan.
keyRequirements: Must be a first-time buyer or fresh start applicant
Property must be vacant or derelict
Must intend to use property as your principal private residence
Income limits apply (same as Local Authority Home Loan)
Works must be approved as part of the application

name: Mortgage Interest Relief
valueSummary: Up to €1,250 (single) or €2,500 (jointly assessed) per tax year — 20% of your interest increase vs 2022
description: A temporary tax relief for homeowners whose mortgage interest payments rose above their 2022 level. You claim 20% of the increase back through your annual tax return. Introduced in Budget 2024 and extended in Budget 2025 to cover the 2024 tax year.
keyRequirements: Mortgage must have been on your principal private residence on 31 December 2022
Mortgage balance must have been between €80,000 and €500,000 at end of 2022
Relief is 20% of the increase in interest paid versus 2022 — you must have paid more interest
Claim via your annual tax return or through myAccount on Revenue.ie
Covers tax years 2023 and 2024

name: Sustainable Energy Communities
valueSummary: Free programme — SEAI funds community energy planning and gives members collective buying power for upgrades
description: A community-based programme where groups of homes, businesses and public buildings plan and deliver energy improvements together. SEAI funds the community group's planning and coordination costs. Individual members still apply for their own SEAI home energy grants but benefit from bulk pricing and shared project management. Over 600 active communities across Ireland.
keyRequirements: Join or form a Sustainable Energy Community group registered with SEAI
Community group must include at least one residential and one community or public building
SEAI provides grant funding to the group for coordination and project development
Individual homeowners apply separately for their own SEAI home energy grants
Search for a community near you at seai.ie/community-energy

name: Housing Adaptation Grant
valueSummary: Up to €30,000 (means tested) — typically covers 80–95% of approved costs
description: A means-tested grant from your local council to adapt your home for a person with a disability or mobility issue. Covers works such as stairlifts, wet rooms, grab rails, access ramps, and structural adaptations. Available nationally but administered and funded by each local authority — availability and waiting times vary by county.
keyRequirements: Applicant or a household member must have a disability or mobility issue
Property must be your principal private residence
Means tested — your household income determines the percentage covered
An occupational therapist assessment is usually required
Application made to your local authority — budgets and waiting lists vary by county
Works must not be started before the grant is approved
